newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late olein buckles under Malaysia fall.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late olein buckles under Malaysia fall.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were lower in late trading on Monday as the market buckled under the pressure of falls in Malaysia, traders said.
They said olein was around 1,370-75 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, down from 1,375-80 rupiah at the opening. Quotes were also heard at 1,365 rupiah.
Malaysian prices continued their downtrend from last Friday as the market consolidated after recent sharp gains.
"Buyers were scare, thanks to the Malaysian market," one trader said. "The falls in Malaysia today, although small, weakened local sentiment and kept buyers away."
Traders said they expected the November export tax on palm olein to be around $19/tonne compared with $30 in October, and around $28 for crude palm oil against $35.28 last month.
An official from the finance ministry said the taxes for this month were expected to be announced later this week.

Data from Belawan Port showed that the MT Wanea left the North Sumatran port on Sunday for Jakarta with 1,000 tonnes of olein. The MT Bum Ju left the port yesterday for Dumai with 2,000 tonnes of palm kernel oil.

The MT Ivy Bank left on Saturday with 2,800 tonnes of olein for Port Klang in Malaysia, while the MT Jo Birk will leave the port for Port Klang on Monday with 1,750 tonnes of fatty acid distillate and 27,000 tonnes of stearin.
The KM Perkasa left for Jakarta with 2,200 tonnes of crude palm oil on Friday.
